artifacts.summary: Mechanically confirms Branch B (streak-accounting defect from alternating trivial/non-trivial Bash calls) via real-transcript replay through the production hook; rules out Branch A for the measured incident while showing the hook does reach a dispatched subagent when it fires; confirms items 2-4 with direct transcript evidence; rules on contract home (external-process-wait.md + bounded-build-waiter.md, rejecting orchestrator-discipline.md) and single-writer mechanism (lake-build-guard.sh flock model).

memory_candidates.content: A dispatched agent (Agent-tool subagent in this harness) records its own transcript at <parent-session-dir>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl, with isSidechain:true entries. PostToolUse hook invocations (and their additionalContext output, when non-empty) are recorded in THAT file, confirming hooks configured in settings.json do fire for, and their additionalContext does reach, a dispatched subagent's own context -- not only the orchestrator's. The exact transcript path for any dispatch is recoverable from its own metrics.jsonl entry's transcript.path field, enabling forensic replay of a real incident's exact command sequence through the real hook binary.

detect-noop-bash.sh's consecutive-trivial-streak counter is defeated by any alternating pattern of one trivial filler call (echo/true/date) and one non-trivial call (e.g. a grep/tail/wc -l log read) in between, since the hook deletes the counter on every non-trivial command. A real 216-call echo-idle incident never reached streak 2, let alone the threshold of 3, confirmed by replaying the real command sequence through the unmodified hook. A streak-threshold design is fragile against exactly the usage pattern (poll-then-filler, repeated) it exists to catch.

lake-build-guard.sh's flock()-based lock-file mechanism (serializing concurrent lake build invocations against one package root, sharing a completed result rather than relaunching) is explicitly documented in its own header as a reusable family convention for a future ...-build-guard.sh sibling. It is the right model to cite for any other shared-tree single-writer requirement (e.g. a test fixture tree raced by two backgrounded suite invocations) rather than inventing a new lock mechanism or falling back to a sentinel-file scheme (which reproduces bounded-build-waiter.md's own documented unwritable-sentinel defect).
